_comment: Tufte-Dracula palette in hex, for Mermaid only. Mermaid's color engine (khroma) throws 'Unsupported color format' on an oklch() string and aborts initialization, so no diagram in the file renders; classDef fill/stroke values choke the flowchart grammar on the literal parens in oklch(...). Every value here is therefore hex: the sRGB rendering of the matching tufte-dracula.css :root oklch() variable, computed through the Oklab -> linear sRGB matrix with gamut clipping (the conversion reproduces the 'was #xxxxxx' hex documented beside each oklch value in tufte-dracula.css). Edit tufte-dracula.css first, then recompute the affected hex here. mermaid.js carries these same values inline because it is inlined verbatim by consumers with no build step; contract-check.yml fails if the two disagree.

init._comment: mermaid.initialize({theme:'base', themeVariables:{darkMode:true, ...}}) in mermaid.js. darkMode has to sit inside themeVariables — mermaidAPI hands only config.themeVariables to base.getThemeVariables(), so a root-level darkMode is never seen by the theme.

classdef._comment: Node-category classDef roles for generators that emit their own 'classDef name fill:...,stroke:...' lines inside a <pre class="mermaid"> block. Not used by mermaid.js itself. Every fill draws from the --data-1..4 ramp, never from the prose accents (--pink, --green, --orange): those already carry a meaning in body copy (h1, inline code, aside bar), and the data ramp exists precisely so a diagram category cannot borrow it. stroke is --purple and color is --surface for every role.
